title: Power industry electrical systems engineer
overviewOfRole: Manage power industry electrical projects, or the operational delivery of power industry work.

knowledges.detail: Core - The electrical power sector, its types of organisations, how they interact, their structure, role and function. Sector regulators, stakeholders and its customers' requirements.
Core - Engineer's role, responsibilities limits of autonomy and coordination with other business functions. Reporting channels within the power sector.
Core - Techniques and approaches for the planning and prioritisation of work tasks, taking into consideration business planning practices, resource planning and management.

Core - Electrical power principles: three phase alternating current and direct current theories; voltage; dynamic and static engineering systems; application of electrical and electronic circuit theory.
Core - Electricity network design, construction, capabilities, complexities, operations and topologies.

Core - Design, operation, function and limitations of transmission or distribution plant and equipment. Substations, transformers, switchgear and auxiliary equipment. Overhead lines. Components that make up the transmission or distribution network.
Core - Electricity network principles of operation in normal and fault conditions. Overhead network, underground network and associated protective devices.
Core - Interfaces between the system voltage control boundaries relevant to the engineer's role or level of authorisation.

Core - Awareness of health and safety regulations relevant to the engineer's role. Construction Design and Management (CDM) requirements. Control of Substances Hazardous to Health (COSHH). Display Screen Equipment. Fire regulations. Health and Safety at Work Act – responsibilities. Managing Health and Safety at Work Regulations. Manual handling. Noise regulation. Provision and use of Work Equipment Regulations (PUWER). Personal Protective Equipment (PPE). Working at height. Reporting of Injuries, Diseases and Dangerous Occurrence Regulations (RIDDOR). Electricity at Work Regulations.
Core - Health and safety procedures and safe systems of work for working on the electrical network, plant and equipment. Electrical safety.
Core - How to carry out safety briefings.
Core - Risk assessments, risk management techniques and approaches, the hierarchy of control. Method statements.
Core - Incident management and emergency procedures.
Core - Awareness of regulatory frameworks, regulatory measures and reporting requirements.
Core - Electricity Safety, Quality and Continuity Regulations (ESQCR).

Core - The impact of low carbon energy on the network.  Environmental regulations and standards: Environmental Protection Act and Hazardous Waste Regulations. The environmental impact of equipment containing SF6. Environmental incidents.
Core - Sustainability principles, design and development considerations. Waste reduction and recycling.
Core - Construction and electrical drawings.
Core - Engineering technical specifications, policies and engineering standards relevant to the role and organisation. What they are and how to use them.
Core - Health, safety and quality management audits and inspections, requirements and approaches.
Core - Awareness and consequence of asset risk, monetised risk process.
Core - Documentation: methods and requirements - electronic and paper.
Core - Report writing and data analysis techniques. Reporting systems.
Core - Problem solving and fault-finding techniques.
Core - Continuous improvement principles and techniques.
Core - Team working principles.
Core - Communication techniques: verbal and written.

Core - Information technology and digital: digital interfaces, email, Management Information Systems (MIS), spreadsheets, presentation, word processing, virtual communication, Artificial Intelligence (AI), learning platforms, work collaboration platforms. General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). General cyber security.
Core - Awareness of network operational cyber security and impact. Network Information Systems Regulations.
Core - Emerging technologies and their impact on projected future load Impact on the network.
Core - Future impact of shifting generation on network topography.
Asset management - Awareness of technical specifications, type registration and design assurance. Asset refurbishment specifications. Asset engineering procedures. Purpose and requirements.
Asset management - Asset management principles, long term network resilience or replacement strategies and objectives. Asset safety, compliance and the impact of business strategy.
Asset management – Appreciation of testing, inspection and maintenance methods and techniques for plant and equipment. Maintenance and inspection plans.
Asset management - Network performance data and analysis techniques.
Asset management - Condition monitoring, asset performance data and analysis techniques. Asset risk assessment, mitigations and constraints applied to assets.
Asset management - Component condition assessments, requirements for re-use, recycling and disposal.
Asset management - Reverse engineering of original materials and analysis techniques. Properties and suitability of materials. The impact on the component and asset.
Asset management - Procedures for the investigation of asset, system or process failure.
Asset management engineer - Plant and equipment proposals.
Electrical project engineer - Awareness of the need for land access. Planning consents and wayleaves for the purpose of land access.
Electrical project engineer - Project planning, implementation and monitoring techniques and approaches.
Electrical project engineer - Procurement and contract management. Contract controls and tendering.
Electrical project engineer - Costings and financial considerations. Budget management.
Electrical project engineer - Resource requirements.
Electrical project engineer - Protection system design, standards and parameters.
Electrical project engineer - Asset security and access requirements.
Electrical project engineer - Work specifications, variations and sign off procedures.
Electrical project engineer - Project team leadership and project coordination techniques and approaches.
Electrical project engineer - Appreciation of construction and installation techniques for underground cables, overhead lines, plant, switchgear, protection and auxiliary equipment.

Electrical project engineer - Appreciation of techniques and requirements for commissioning overhead lines, underground cables, plant, switchgear, protection and auxiliary equipment. Testing sequences.
Operational delivery engineer - Procedures for the management of control boundaries.
Operational delivery engineer - Operation of electricity system apparatus on the electricity network.
Operational delivery engineer - Operational delivery work planning.

Operational delivery engineer - Receiving, preparation, issue, transfer and cancellation of safety documents. Permit to Work, Limitation of Access and Sanction for Test. When they are used and requirements for briefing recipients.
Operational delivery engineer - Contractor management and considerations for the management of contractors working on engineering projects. Tendering processes and contractual arrangements.
Operational delivery engineer – Managing and directing working parties, issuing work instructions.
Operational delivery engineer – Monitoring procedures for work activities and equipment, approaches for monitoring budget and timescales.
Operational delivery engineer - Pre-energisation checks for electricity system equipment relevant to the role.
Operational delivery engineer - Asset management records for decommissioning, commissioning, maintenance and alterations to the network. Procedures and regulatory requirements.

behaviours.detail: Take responsibility for health and safety.
Collaborate with others for example, within teams, across disciplines, and external stakeholders, promoting inclusion.
Take responsibility for the quality of work. For example, decisive, self-reliant, and motivated.
Respond and adapt to work demands and situations.
Committed to maintaining and enhancing competence of self and others through Continued Professional Development (CPD).

Core - Apply health and safety policies, procedures and electricity network safe systems of work.
Core - Carry out safety briefings for staff and contractors on site.
Core - Undertake the risk assessment required for the task and apply the hierarchy of control.
Core - Follow emergency and incident response procedures.
Core - Comply with regulations and manage work to meet regulatory and legislative requirements.
Core - Apply environmental and sustainability procedures in compliance with regulations, standards and guidelines.
Core - Read and interpret technical specifications.
Core - Interpret and use construction and electrical system diagrams and drawings.
Core - Carry out health, safety and quality audits and inspections.
Core - Evaluate the risk and system impact of work options to support business decisions.
Core - Complete required documentation for the work activity.
Core - Complete technical reports.
Core - Collect record and interpret internal and external data and information. Use information and data to support business decisions.
Core - Apply problem solving or fault-finding techniques.
Core - Use continuous improvement techniques and make recommendations for the optimisation of systems or processes.
Core - Apply teamworking principles.
Core - Communicate verbally and in writing with others for example, colleagues, contractors and stakeholders. Matching technique to audience.
Core - Establish and maintain productive working relationships, for example with colleagues, contractors or stakeholders.
Core - Use information and digital technology. Comply with GDPR and cyber security regulations and policies.

cluster: Quality improvement and project control manager
clusterDescription: Maintain and improve the integrity and quality of complex products and processes, improve whole production and process technologies, and the overall health and safety of the working environment

duties.dutyDetail: Communicate complex information and manage relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
Ensure the health and safety of those working on or near the electrical power network.
Oversee the completion of work tasks to meet regulatory, environmental and legislative requirements.
Manage risks and implement control measures or contingency planning where necessary.
Contribute to the continuous improvement of assets, processes or systems.
Monitor asset and component condition and performance to inform maintenance planning.
Contribute to the development of long term strategic asset maintenance planning.
Develop asset maintenance, inspection and refurbishment plans.
Contribute to the investigation of asset, system or process failure.
Manage the delivery of electrical projects. Ensuring work is delivered on time, on budget and to specification.
Lead and brief an electrical project team, ensuring the safety of staff and contractors and the security of resources and assets.
Plan and organise electrical maintenance and installation work.
Manage staff and contractors working on the electricity network.
